bug_semantics: CVE-2025-25034 / GHSA-wcx8-f39f-5c87 describe unauthenticated PHP object injection (CWE-502) in SugarCRM: unsanitized rest_data is passed to unserialize() in SugarRestSerialize.php, enabling RCE. The assigned repository is rapid7/metasploit-framework, which does not ship SugarCRM or that sink; it only contains a public exploit module that targets SugarCRM.
flaw_origin: Not present in rapid7/metasploit-framework. CVE.org (PUBLISHED, assigner VulnCheck) lists affected product SugarCRM across 6.5/6.7/7.5/7.6 branches; NVD status is Deferred, not rejected. GHSA-wcx8-f39f-5c87 is unreviewed, withdrawn_at=null, vulnerabilities=[], no GitHub package. The only clone path matching advisory references is modules/exploits/unix/webapp/sugarcrm_rest_unserialize_exec.rb, an exploit added 2016-09-07 as df5fdbff41a0e9464eddcb8b4172cf49fa21e40f ('Add module for KIS-2016-07'), later annotated with CVE-2025-25034 in fd21209e4d38ca374b40b4d7963bed7b7ccc5821. No SugarRestSerialize.php exists in this repo.

evidence: CVE record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2025-25034: state=PUBLISHED, title='SugarCRM PHP Deserialization RCE', affected vendor/product=SugarCRM/SugarCRM. NVD: vulnStatus=Deferred, source=disclosure@vulncheck.com; description names SugarCRM SugarRestSerialize.php rest_data unserialize. GHSA-wcx8-f39f-5c87: type=unreviewed, withdrawn_at=null, vulnerabilities=[], github_reviewed=null. Clone HEAD e698ea413163b31759d78603e5018552bf14ae8e contains only the Metasploit exploit module at modules/exploits/unix/webapp/sugarcrm_rest_unserialize_exec.rb; git log --all -- '**/SugarRestSerialize.php' is empty. This assigned-repo mapping is a false positive: the advisory is not a security issue in metasploit-framework. Upstream traced: the true affected product is SugarCRM Community Edition (proprietary after CE 6.5.x; KIS-2016-07). Public git mirrors (bkilgore/sugarcrm_dev 6.2.0beta 2011; m2osw/sugarcrm 6.5.25 2017) are squashed release imports with no fine-grained history, so no BIC/AI attribution is possible. Vulnerable line verified in 6.2.0beta service/core/REST/SugarRestSerialize.php: `$data = unserialize(from_html($data))` on $_REQUEST['rest_data']; fixed in 6.5.24/6.5.25 by `sugar_unserialize()`. Funnel row was a repo mis-mapping: the GHSA (vulnerabilities=[]) cited only a metasploit exploit module URL, which selection mistook for the affected repo. This campaign audits rapid7/metasploit-framework, which ships only the exploit module — no vulnerable product code exists here.

Basis: Disposition re-verified: CVE-2025-25034 PUBLISHED but advisory describes SugarCRM SugarRestSerialize.php — a product not present in rapid7/metasploit-framework; metasploit ships a module FOR the vulnerability, not the vulnerability. Advisory-repo mismatch = advisory wrong for this repo. Original analysis retained for provenance: Vulnerability-first tracing separates the affected application from the repository merely hosting a working exploit. The request path, bypass, gadget, and version lifecycle are concrete: old SugarCRM directly deserialized rest_data; 6.5.23 added an object-header regex that missed O:+14:; the Metasploit module demonstrates that bypass; and 6.5.24 broadened the regex at the first-party documented fixed boundary. However, rapid7/metasploit-framework first received only the exploit in df5fdbff41a0e9464eddcb8b4172cf49fa21e40f after the fix. The official SugarCRM public repository contains no historical source, and the available forks begin with initial snapshots or whole-release imports. Those imports can show first appearance within a mirror and parent absence there, but the protocol explicitly excludes release aggregates and imported snapshots from being a BIC. Consequently the smallest true SugarCRM introducer, its immediate parent, and the granular SugarCRM fix commit cannot be proven. With no BIC commit object, AI attribution cannot be inspected or inferred, so a closed NOT_AI or AI verdict would be unsupported; the removed vendor history is a genuine public-history boundary and warrants BLOCKED.
